**Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member onboarding**: no standardised first-contact-to-first-class journey; risk of inconsistent experience, missed upsell, poor retention setup
- **Churn & cancellation**: no documented trigger points, win-back protocol, or exit interview process—bleeding members without data
- **Coaching standards & quality audit**: no baseline for what "good coaching" looks like across classes; no audit mechanism or feedback loop to coaches
- **Member check-ins & milestone tracking**: no scheduled touchpoints post-onboarding; 30-day goals and outcomes sit orphaned
- **Complaints & incidents**: no escalation path, documentation standard, or resolution SOP (crucial for duty of care in fitness)
- **Pause & freeze management**: no protocol for member pause requests, duration rules, or re-engagement trigger
- **Supplies & inventory**: ordering, stock levels, reorder triggers undefined—operational blind spot
- **Data privacy & GDPR**: no documented data handling, consent capture, or retention/deletion process (legal exposure)
- **Referral programme**: mechanics, tracking, reward distribution undefined

**Needs updating**

- **Coaches 20/24**: missing "Weekly Key Coach Tasks"—what does a coach actually *do* Monday–Friday? (roster, prep, feedback, admin?)
- **Coaching Development Roadmap**: no progression pathway for coaches; unclear how they level up or move to senior/lead roles
- **Marketing 5/5**: likely missing retention/win-back workflows (email sequences, member re-engagement campaigns) that sit between marketing and ops
- **Clients 23/33**: "Transformation Pillars" and "Member Outcomes" not linked to reporting—how do you measure retention drivers?
- **New Quarter Program Launch**: no launch SOP; risk of chaotic rollout, mixed messaging, missed revenue window

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

• **Start with your revenue breakdown, not imagination.** Pull last month's actual transactions. What are members paying for NOW (classes, PT, packages, drop-ins)? What's fuzzy pricing? Build your menu around what's already working and what's leaking money through inconsistent rates.

• **Create TWO menus with different language.** Coaches need the nuts-and-bolts version (class capacity limits, PT session length, cancellation policy, upsell triggers). Members get the benefits-forward version ("Transform in 8 weeks" not "16 sessions at £20"). Same info, different sell.

• **Price visibly, not hidden.** List everything with cost. A common trap: "classes included" sounds good but kills PT sales. Be explicit: "Unlimited classes + 1 PT session/month £X" forces members to see what they're actually getting and makes upselling the second PT session obvious.

• **Field-test with your best 3 coaches first.** Give them the draft menu. They'll spot what's missing, what confuses members mid-session, and what actually sells. One 15-min conversation saves you a reprint.

• **Post it where money changes hands** — at sign-up, on your app, at the desk. Not in a PDF nobody reads. Make pricing the default conversation, not the thing members have to ask about.

What's your current pricing situation — is it consistent across all members, or is it a mess of legacy deals?

**Insights**

• **July was a breakthrough month that August has failed to sustain.** You found a formula in July—probably a creative, audience segment, or offer—that dropped CPL to £2 and drove 29 sales (13.5% close rate). August's 50 leads at £3 CPL suggests you've either lost access to that winning audience, paused the winning creative, or diluted spend across underperforming campaigns. The close rate jumped to 32%, so your offer is still strong; the problem is lead volume and consistency.

• **Your unit economics only work at scale.** At £3 CPL and 32% close, you're hitting £19 income per lead. But that's razor-thin. April–June showed you can't sustain this business at £6–£21 CPL. You need to get back to July's £2 CPL or lower, or close rate needs to stay at 32%+ consistently. Right now August looks like luck, not system.

• **April–June (zero sales) means your targeting or creative was completely misaligned.** You were burning £1,374 to build a cold audience that didn't convert. July's shift to 215 leads suggests you either switched to a warm audience (email list, website visitors, page engagers) or nailed a demographic/interest combo. August's collapse to 50 leads says you've gone too narrow or killed the winning lever.

**Actions**

1. **Audit your July winning campaign immediately.** Pull the exact audience, creative, placement, and offer from July. If it's still active, analyse why lead volume dropped 77%. If you paused it, restart at £20–30/day and scale slowly. If you changed it, revert. This is your control group.

2. **Rebuild your warm audience pipeline.** The jump from 20 leads (Jun) to 215 (Jul) almost certainly means you found a warm segment—website visitors, email subscribers, or Page engagers. Build three custom audiences: (a) website visitors last 30 days, (b) email subscribers, (c) people who've engaged with 3+ posts. Test a £5/day budget on each with your July creative. Don't spray and pray
